- **`claude-mem server jobs retry` no longer reports `requeued` for a job it did not publish** (#6439, thanks @HEOJUNFO). If Redis was unreachable, or the shell had no `CLAUDE_MEM_QUEUE_ENGINE=bullmq`, the command printed `"outcome": "requeued"` and exited 0, and the job never ran. It now moves the row back to `failed` with `retry_republish_failed`, prints the reason and exits 1, so the same command works once the queue is reachable.

### Installer improvements

- On phones, **Set up my agents** stays within reach while you review the detected tools or expand the agent list.
- A fresh installation shows how many agents you set up and what Cloud Sync can remember across devices. Setup only offers scan details when it has results or a reading error to show.

### Cloud Sync setup

- Select **Try Cloud Sync free for 30 days** from your focus areas to open monthly checkout. The trial requires a card and costs $0 today, then $12/month after 30 days.
- Setup preselects detected agents. You can discover your recent work or start with your next session. Annual Cloud Sync ($99 upfront) and free local setup are available before checkout. If you already have Cloud Sync, connect your device with your existing plan.
- After Cloud Sync activates, setup shows token usage fro

### Standalone Cloud Sync in the installer

- Run `npx claude-mem install` and choose Cloud Sync to connect your devices while keeping your current memory provider. The monthly plan requires a card and includes a full 30-day trial, followed by $12 per month. The annual plan costs $99 upfront.
- The installer carries your chosen plan into checkout and verifies that cmem.ai confirms the same offer. Hosted tokens are a separate, optional purchase. Existing bundled Pro setups keep their saved settings.
- You ca

- **`/api/advisor-calls` caps its offset like every other listing** (#6396, thanks @DeryFerd). A huge `offset` made SQLite scan and discard rows on the worker's shared connection. It now uses the shared listing cap, and a viewer that keeps paging stops with `offsetCapReached`.

- **The unauthenticated `/v1/info` no longer shows Redis error text** (#6380, thanks @DeryFerd). A queue lane that could not be read used to publish the driver's error, such as a host and port. The reason now stays in the server log.

- **My Work refresh prefers MXC for isolated Codex launches on Windows** (#6348, thanks @QuantScorpus, refs #5163). The refresh no longer picks the unelevated sandbox and fails before the agent starts.

- **A JSON key ending with `_` no longer makes `toCamel` and `toPascal` throw** (#1313). With `transform: postgres.camel`, such a key made the whole query throw. The trailing `_` is now kept, so `a_` stays `a_`, and an empty key stays empty instead of becoming `undefined`.

- **Node.js 18** is supported again: `engines` is `>=18` and CI runs it. Nothing in Postgres.js needs 20; `using`, `await using` and tracing are used where the runtime has them. Loading it with `require` still needs Node.js 20.19 or 22.12.
- **`PGSSLMODE` is read** (#1307). It was ignored, so `PGSSLMODE=verify-full` connected in plain text without an error. This may change how existing setups connect: `require` now uses TLS and fails against a server without it, and `verify-ca` and `verify-full` check the c

- **A NUL character in a connection parameter can no longer add parameters** (also in v3). A `database`, `user` or `connection` value such as `'db\0user\0postgres'` was sent as further startup parameters, so an app that put untrusted input there, as with a database per tenant, could be made to log in as another user where that user needs no password, or with `replication` or `options` set. A NUL in any protocol string, also in query text and identifiers, now rejects with `NUL_CHARACTER`.

# Version 1.1.0 revision notes

This additive post-acquisition supplement publishes 32 earlier unpublished supporting syscall trials within the same study. Their 28 September 2026 collection dates and four separate eight-trial denominators are explicit. They remain pilot evidence, never pooled with the registered campaign.

The manuscript now states acquisition timestamps relative to registration, maps each family to its acquisition filesystem, highlights the 0/40 ACK-marker dependent-prefix result and the

Original scientific records were copied byte-for-byte, and all 95 cells and 43 registered comparisons were independently recomputed before publication. Prior pilots, qualification observations, full disk images, credentials and private transfer maps are excluded. Dependent log-prefix reconstructions add zero scientific units.

## Website Forms

- **Your website's own form, sending to Crewtavo.** Install **Apps → Crewtavo - Website Forms**, copy your form's address into its action, and each message becomes a request and an email to up to five people. Reply to the email and you're answering the customer. It works like Formspree: `_gotcha`, `_subject`, `_next` and `_replyto` work the same, so a Formspree form moves over by changing its address.
- **On the right client.** Messages are matched to clients by email, then phone. A clie

- **Prices from your real ABC account.** Looking up a price or searching ABC's catalog failed on production accounts with "ABC Supply couldn't use that." ABC's pricing needs every request to carry a request ID, which its docs call optional and its sandbox doesn't ask for. Crewtavo now sends one with every price request.

## Improved Logging

- **ABC Supply says why.** When ABC Supply can't use a price lookup or a search, the message now gives ABC's own reason instead of only "ABC Supply couldn't use that."
- **The whole answer in the server's log.** Anything ABC Supply turns down is written to the server's log with what was asked (account, branch and items, never your keys), so a problem can be traced without guessing.

- Images on other sites in a report are shown as a link ("Image from <host>: <alt text>") instead of being loaded, so opening a report no longer tells another site who opened it, and an agent cannot make reviewers' browsers call arbitrary addresses. The content security policy now allows images only from verifair itself and `data:`.

### Changed

- Text written by an agent is labelled in notifications. The review email's excerpt is headed "Judge this (written by the agent, not checked by verif

### Security

- Comment anchoring no longer slows down sharply on huge, repetitive sections, so an agent-written report cannot stall the pages that show it. When the exact quoted context is gone after an edit, only the first 200 matches of the quote are compared, so in very repetitive text a moved comment can land on an earlier match.
- Local mode refuses web pages on dotted hostnames other than the one in `VERIFAIR_BASE_URL` (400 `Unknown host`), which blocks DNS-rebinding attacks from websites you visit.

### Fixed

- A heading inside a plan or report overlapped itself when it wrapped on a phone.
- On phones the verdict bar took about a quarter of the screen. The summary box is now one line that grows when you tap it, and is hidden when you cannot give a verdict.
- On phones the new agent token was cut off in its box; it now wraps so you can see all of it.
- Small buttons, comment label chips and "comment" links are at least 32px tall on phones.
- The project name in the phone breadcrumb is no longer squeeze

### Added

- Each version tag creates a GitHub release, with this changelog's section as its notes.

### Changed

- The theme switch is now a small icon control (monitor, sun, moon) next to **Sign out**, with a tooltip and a screen-reader label on each option.
